title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s Valentine’s Day [1]
text: Although the subtitle mentions Valentine’s Day, there aren’t any Valentine’s Day-related elements in the story yet.

It’s been a little over a month since Christmas—time has flown by in the blink of an eye, and now it’s February… Is that right? Oh well, it’s February now. By the way, the New Year’s holidays were pretty hectic in their own right. It turns out this world has a New Year’s celebration too, so I went to the nearest church for my first visit of the year.

“Why a church?” “Isn’t it supposed to be a shrine?” I thought to myself, but since the Hero is the object of worship—and he’s the one who popularized the New Year’s tradition—it seems to be the custom in this other world to make the first visit of the year to a church. By the way, I handed out some New Year’s money to the villagers. I didn’t put it in red envelopes; I just gave it to them straight up, and they complained that it lacked atmosphere.

Speaking of Japanese style—or rather, a woman who wears kimono all the time—I’m reminded of Glass. I thought someone who’d look perfect for New Year’s might show up… but she didn’t. I’d completely forgotten, but she went missing a while after the world was saved. She’s apparently not dead, but I wonder what she’s up to these days…
By the way, I’ve just arrived at the Robin Hoods’ hideout in disguise.
“This way, sir.”

It’s been a few months now since I started using the Shadow as a messenger to give orders to the Robin Hoods, hasn’t it? Right now, the former thieves I’ve taken under my wing are steadily expanding their hideout while delivering solid results.

First, the former thief-turned-righteous bandit—who became my slave and went through the Class Up process with my guidance—used his physical strength to become a famous thief in a region outside my territory. Drawing on that strength, he gathered his scattered comrades to establish a bandit hideout. Operating under the purpose of being a righteous bandit and the policy of stealing only from unscrupulous merchants, he works with his comrades to amass wealth and distributes it to gain the support of the people. Since then, he has avoided targeting the carriages under my jurisdiction as much as possible and, as a “sharp-nosed” Robin Hood, has gained fame throughout the region. I’ve received reports from my spies that his ranks are growing exponentially.

Thanks to acting exactly as I instructed, this Robin Hood has become an overnight sensation. It’s been a while since I’ve seen him, but I imagine he’s still wearing that same ambiguous expression. Today, I’m holding a secret meeting at the Robin Hood Guild. By the way, I’ll be meeting separately from Raphtalia and the other slaves. Well… it’s not like I’m doing anything particularly praiseworthy, and I figure they’d just nag me anyway.

I was led to the entrance of a hideout built in a corner of a town’s underground waterway. It was a place that reeked terribly, and just as it looked, it was home to the kind of people who’d be too embarrassed to show their faces in public. A thief from the Robin Hood Guild who was standing guard glared at me the moment he saw me.
“…What’s the password?”
“Katsudon-like.”
…What kind of password is that!? I think that every single time. Is that Righteous Thief just trying to harass me? Well, I’ve exploited them enough that I guess I deserve a snide remark or two.
“Tch! Come in.”

Just as I thought he’d clicked his tongue, the guard opened the hideout’s entrance and motioned for me to go in. I threw on my robe to hide my face and stepped inside. The atmosphere inside the Robin Hood Guild… well, since they’re a bunch of roughnecks to begin with, it’s not exactly pleasant. As soon as I step inside, I find myself in a place that feels like a tavern, where a bunch of thieves posing as Robin Hoods are making a racket. Following the Shadow’s lead, I make my way to the bar counter and place my order with the bartender.
“Milk on the rocks.”
The bartender flinches slightly and stares at me…
“How sweet?”
“Extra sweet, I’d say.”

At Shadow’s reply, the bartender sighs and steps aside to let us pass toward the back of the counter. Seriously, can’t we do something about that code phrase? What the heck is “milk on the rocks”? Does he plan to make it extra sweet—turn it into condensed milk or something?

Shadow and I walked straight into the back of the tavern. Beyond that was a long hallway, and we made our way deeper into the hideout. I thought, “This is a hassle…” but I suppose it’s important to remain on high alert. If I recall correctly… the people who are only allowed into the tavern at the entrance are the ones with low credibility, and the further back you go, the more credibility the organization seems to have.

Eventually, we arrived at a luxurious room at the very back. Sitting there, waiting for us, were the thief I knew—the boss of the Righteous Thieves’ Guild—along with a slave trader and a jewelry merchant. While carefully scanning the area, I took off my robe.
“Well, well, it’s the Shield Hero himself. Hello.”
“Hehehe, how are you feeling?”
“…It’s been a while. The Shield Hero.”
Each of them gave me a brief greeting. Today, we’re scheduled to hold our regular gathering at the Thieves’ Guild.
“It hasn’t really been that long… How are you guys doing?”
“We’re doing quite well, actually. Yes.”
“That’s a pointless conversation with a merchant. Hehehe…”
“Ah, yeah… We’ve reached our target amount from the money we’ve extorted from nobles and merchants.”

As I asked each of them how they were doing—the same old conversation we always have—I took my seat. Kage was eavesdropping at the entrance to the room. It would be a real pain if the thieves got wind of our conversation.
“Well then, let’s begin today’s meeting. Yes.”

The slave trader raises his hand and gives a progress report. Even if the world is saved, as long as people exist, darkness—or rather, that inescapable negative side—won’t disappear. Even if Melty takes the lead in unifying the world and holds summit meetings among the leaders of various nations on the surface to stop the conflict, she can’t completely stop it behind the scenes.
After all, even Melromarc has a history of enslaving Demi-Humans. Although the situation has eased somewhat in the present, people’s perceptions remain deeply ingrained.

That’s right—just because the world has become peaceful doesn’t mean slavery will disappear. The idea that slavery would suddenly be abolished and all humanity would become equal is far too naive. The desire for a labor force that can be easily exploited is universal, no matter where you go. Moreover, it’s easy to imagine that once the world merges and a war is fought against another world, the victorious side will inevitably resort to looting.

It’s been only a few days since we defeated that damn goddess… yet reports have already come in that some people have resorted to looting—a familiar enough reality. The idea that “if you win, you can do whatever you want” is just too naive. What’s more, these are precisely the kind of people who, when you ask if they even fought properly, are highly suspect.
“According to an investigation by the Dark Guild of Zeltoble, slaves from countries in the fused world—”

The slave trader begins explaining to me, documents in hand. I don’t particularly intend to abolish slavery itself. There are surely people who end up as slaves due to family circumstances or poverty.

Rather than banishing them in the name of “freedom” and killing them brutally… there might still be a chance for them to survive. There are as many reasons as there are people, and rejecting the idea outright won’t get us anywhere. After all, there’s not much difference between slavery and forcing people into hard labor by tying them down with money.

Come to think of it, even in modern Japan, there are people doing backbreaking, unrewarding labor just like slaves. I’d like to see things improve, but no matter how many talented people there are, there are plenty of things in this world that are simply beyond our control. That wouldn’t change even if the world were saved.
“To get straight to the point, the slave community is expanding, but the likelihood of it getting a bit out of hand is increasing.”
“Hmm…”

To summarize the slave trader’s explanation: The world on the other side of the Glass has been thoroughly ravaged by that shitty goddess. What’s more, it seems there are quite a few people in our world who view it as a country that started a war and lost. Those guys are barbarians. You can do whatever you want to them. More and more people are taking to slave hunting with a frontier spirit, seeking resources from such uncivilized lands.

At the top of the list are Shieldfreeden and the former Kingdom of Faubrey. These are the nations that declared war on Melromarc and its allied nations, were defeated, and were ordered to pay enormous reparations. It’s utterly appalling that they would try to cover their own responsibilities by invading other countries. It’s truly sad to see this as the end result of those who championed freedom and equality and claimed to stand for justice.

Ultimately, they’ve completely misunderstood the meaning of freedom. Waging war… is a freedom, but it does not grant the freedom to shirk responsibility when you lose. Freedom without responsibility is nothing more than sheer selfishness.

The problem is that since they aren’t acting openly, there’s nothing Melty can do about it. It’s obvious that even if she complained, she’d just be brushed off. In fact, they are paying what they’re required to pay, so from Melty’s standpoint, she can’t really bring it up. It’s not that there’s no way to force the issue, but there are limits either way.

Just when I thought the world had become peaceful and a little more decent, here we go again. This world is still as rotten as ever. It’s not something that’ll be fixed anytime soon. So if the other side is operating behind the scenes, we’ll have to do the same. Anyway, the problem is that the defeated nations of our world are secretly engaging in slave raids and plundering other countries to boost their economies.
“What about you?”
I ask the jewelry dealer for a similar report.
“It’s much the same. There are a lot of rare items, antiques, and works of art from over there flowing into the black market.”
“It’s a lamentable state of affairs.”

The victor is the government; the vanquished are the rebels. It’s like kicking a dead man… If they think it’s okay to take anything from the losing side, they’re being way too naive. Still, when it comes to rare items, it’s understandable that more people would want them.
“However… since similar works of art already exist in this world, they’re difficult to authenticate, so their prices haven’t risen that much.”
“I see.”

That’s right… even in this world’s civilization, there are quite a few items similar to those found in the Glass World. It’s a bit of a fusion of Japanese and Western styles, after all. I hear there are even Japanese-style items in Eastern countries.

The Glass World tends to have a fairly Japanese-style aesthetic. I wonder what to make of elves and dwarves wearing kimonos? Well, I guess I shouldn’t let it bother me. There are plenty of other races, after all. In that sense, the slave trade involving rare races must be thriving.

…Of course, it seems there are people like that in this world, too—collectors. However, just like monster collectors, the goal of Demi-Human collectors is collection, not killing. It’s just a problem if they die. …Though it’s a whole different story if they’re gathering taxidermy specimens—that’s downright nasty. Anyway, back to the topic at hand: gathering exotic items… It’s scary to think prices might skyrocket.
“Hey. You know what’s going on, right?”
I glare at the former thief-turned-Robin Hood. He’s been swept up in the tension and remained silent, but then he gave a slight nod.
“Yeah, the plan was for us to raid and confiscate the goods from the guys trying to funnel those kinds of items into Zeltoble’s black market auction, right?”

“That’s right. Gather as many of the high-value items as possible… and dispose of them. We need to make them feel the risk of stealing—or rather, of letting them circulate. Worst-case scenario, we’ll send out a Hero.”

Currently, we’re sending Itsuki, Rishia, and the others to protect the world of Glass from those who are attempting theft or slave raids. In a sense, they’re the obvious villains. Before even considering that they might have their own reasons—and feeling sympathy for them—plunder is simply evil.

We can ask them for their reasons after we’ve captured them. Well, it’s difficult to capture them without killing them whenever possible, though. If the plundering becomes too conspicuous, the Heroes will openly conduct inspections and mete out punishment.
“They’ve been stopped for now, but who knows what’ll happen down the road.”

The atmosphere grows heavy at the Robin Hood’s words. There are more than enough people out there who won’t stop even if the Heroes tell them to. It might appeal to the otaku sensibility—how the darker the night, the brighter the light—but it’s hardly a good situation.
“So, for the time being, we plan to prioritize security while coordinating with the Dark Guild of Zeltoble to bring the situation under control.”
“What are you planning to do?”
“First, we’ll make them establish a rule within the underworld that slave hunting is a shameful act. Well, it’ll probably be tough, though.”
The underworld has its own rules. If you cross this line, you’ll be labeled the scum of the underworld. Once that happens, the barrier to committing crimes will skyrocket.

Well, establishing this rule will be difficult. Even the Dark Guild is currently at a loss regarding how to handle this unknown race. If they were to attempt slave hunting while the Hero is keeping a close watch, it would put the Dark Guild itself in danger… We’ll maneuver things so they come to believe that. By doing this, we’ll get the Dark Guild to propose the rule themselves and make them feel like they’re walking a tightrope.

It might be profitable. But the risk is way too high. That’s why even the Dark Guild considers it a punishable offense. We need to make sure the Dark Guild’s assassination squad gets involved to lighten the Hero’s burden. We have to make sure that happens.
I’ll probably have to work this out with the Bow Hero… Itsuki and Rishia, I suppose.
“Yes, we’ve already understood the Hero’s intentions in advance and are acting accordingly. Yes.”
The slave trader’s willingness to cooperate is downright scary.
“I am well aware of just how terrifying it is to conduct business while making the Heroes your enemies. Yes.”
“Well, that’s about it. We’re not going to abolish slavery itself. The problem is forcibly rounding up slaves through slave raids.”

It’s a well-known fact even in the countries of my world that engaging in such practices turns a place into a melting pot of races and could end up being a noose around one’s own neck. It might sound strange coming from me, but slaves are human… right? Well, maybe they don’t count as humans—maybe they fall under the category of Demi-Humans or humanoid races?
“Oh? Given the Shield Hero’s position, wouldn’t aiming for abolition be fitting for a hero?”
“That’s exactly why it’s impossible from my position. If someone else wants to lead the movement to abolish slavery, let them do it. But now is not the time.”

…… To begin with, there’s no way I—the Shield Hero, who’s been working those slaves to the bone all this time—could possibly call for the abolition of slavery. I never had any intention of doing that from the start, anyway.
“Just as the Hero said… the times are beginning to change, aren’t they? Yes.”

Well, that’s about right. The darkness of this world revolves around me, the Hero who saved it. If I were to say white is black, white would become black. But since that’s not how it works, I’ll do “black” things within the limits of what the public doesn’t hear about.

Besides, it’s best to minimize any obstacles that might arise from cultural exchange as much as possible. Conflicts might break out in the future, but for now, our duty is to create an era where there are more happy people.

Well, it feels pretty contradictory coming from me—someone who won’t abolish slavery—but a certain degree of compromise is necessary. We can’t make everyone happy. That’s why we’re taking action to create an era where as many people as possible are happy.
That is the role of us heroes who remain in this world.

The burden of that title is heavier than you might imagine. It’s convenient to use, and it’s quite comfortable, but it has its drawbacks. Those in the position of a hero are expected to act like heroes. So, even though it’s not really my style, I have to act like a hero. Since I’m reaping the benefits, I can’t really complain. It’s a hassle in many ways, though.
“Well then, shall we continue?”

And so, we carefully discussed specific strategies afterward. The presence of the accessory merchant serves both as a money-making opportunity and as a way to help us identify dangerous areas we shouldn’t venture into. He’s well aware of this, too, and has compiled a list of dangerous goods through his own connections with merchant acquaintances. Well, the issues regarding slave hunting and looting had already been largely settled.
Since it’s going to be tough to post as frequently as I did around Christmas due to various circumstances, I think I’ll stick to daily updates for a while.
